tutorial.title: Learn the hex board

steps.welcome: Win by being the last king in play. Three armies start on different edges of a 91-cell hexagon. White goes first, then Black, then Red.
steps.white: White’s pawns advance away from White’s edge. Move the pawn from d10 to d9.
steps.black: Black’s pawns advance in a different direction. Move the pawn from j4 to i5.
steps.red: Red faces the third direction. Move the pawn from d4 to e4.
steps.pieces: Rooks follow hex edges, bishops follow corners, and queens do both. Kings take a single rook or bishop step. Knights jump two steps in one direction and one along a neighboring direction. Pawns capture on their two forward flanks.
steps.promote: At the far boundary, a pawn can become a queen, rook, bishop or knight. Move f2 to f1 and choose a knight.
steps.mate: Checkmate eliminates a player and leaves their remaining pieces as blockers. Red is already out. Move White’s queen from i1 to g2 to mate Black and win.
steps.stalemate: What happens when a player has no legal move and their king is safe?

tutorial.wrong: That’s a different answer. Try again.
tutorial.summary: You’ve practiced the three pawn directions, promotion and checkmate.

rules.board: The board has six sides and 91 hexagonal cells. Players start on alternating edges.
rules.turns: White moves, then Black, then Red. Each army’s pawns advance in its own direction.
rules.pieces: Rooks follow edges and bishops follow corners. Knights jump two steps in one direction and one step along a neighboring direction. Kings can take one rook or bishop step. Pawns advance one cell, capture to either forward flank, and promote on the far boundary.
rules.elimination: Checkmate takes a player out. Their pieces become still blockers. The last king wins.
